newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Police to review handling of NZ mass murder case.
newsitem.headline: Police to review handling of NZ mass murder case.

text.p: New Zealand police said on Tuesday they had appointed a senior officer to review police handling of evidence against convicted mass murderer David Bain.
Bain was convicted for killing his parents, two sisters and a brother with a .22 rifle in Dunedin in 1994. He was jailed for life, with a minimum sentence of 16 years.

But the conviction of the 25 year-old music student has always had its doubters. Publication this month of a book on the case by former All Black rugby fullback Joe Karam has stirred up the controversy.
Police Commissioner Peter Doone said the review would be carried out because of concern about criticism of the police investigation in Karam's book, "David and Goliath".
Karam welcomed the inquiry but said it would have had more credibility if it was carried out by an independent body, not the police.
Auckland police commander Assistant Commissioner Brion Duncan was appointed to conduct the review.
Karam said in his book that the father, Robin Bain, shot his family in an attempt to hide details of an incestuous affair with daughter Laniet, evidence that was suppressed in the trial.

"I just hope it is done with the objectivity Peter Doone has suggested it will be," Karam said. "But if the inquiry comes back supporting the police investigation, I doubt whether the public will be satisfied.
"I have had a former top detective look at the case and he has listed 12 serious deficiencies in the manner in which police conducted their investigation in the first four days.
"Four of these had the potential to, or did in fact, disadvantage David Bain."
A David Bain defence team, which includes Karam, will soon seek to have Bain pardoned under a section of the Crimes Act which caters for prerogatives of mercy.
The application will be made to the Governor-General Sir Michael Hardie Boys, who could refer the case to the Cabinet.
